audience: Applicants need to maintain accurate credentials, prepare for testing and distinguish knowledge-test rules from skills-test rules.
accuracy: No passing percentage is inferred from the missed-question allowance. The skills-test score, entry inspection cutoff and automatic-failure conditions are separate rules. Fee amounts and contradictory lost-credential service channels remain debt.
dynamic: Current service methods, extension fees, examiner contact routes, availability of test languages and Selective Service guidance require current official verification before live applicant advice.
marketAngle: test preparation, document readiness and licensing follow-through
mis: Finishing a skills test successfully does not itself authorize driving before the results are recorded and the license is issued.
mnemonic: Prepare, demonstrate and record is a teaching reminder for the skills-test sequence.
glossary: A duplicate replaces an existing credential; a restriction limits permitted driving; a critical driving error ends the skills test with failure.
skills: Prepare the skills-test vehicle and documents
debts: Physical page thirty allows an office or online duplicate application, while physical page thirty-one says lost-credential residents must visit an office; clarify applicable cases before giving service-channel advice.
The knowledge-test language list is an availability claim requiring a current official check before a live booking decision.
The federal Selective Service paragraph on physical page twenty-eight is outside passenger-car knowledge instruction and needs current federal verification before use.
C: An applicant may request a medical-condition notation on the credential to alert people helping during an emergency.
A permanent-disability notation requires a permanent qualifying impairment certified in writing by a licensed physician, physician assistant or advanced-practice professional nurse.
A permanent-disability notation also requires ITD to determine that the applicant meets the remaining credential requirements.
A person with a non-expiring disability placard or disability plate may present its registration to request the permanent-disability credential notation.
To change the credential name, an applicant must request a duplicate or make the change during an eligible renewal.
A credential name change requires legal evidence such as an Idaho-standard certified marriage record, a court-certified divorce decree or court documents.
The name held by the Social Security Administration must be updated before applying for the duplicate credential.
A change of address must be reported to ITD within thirty days.
A changed address appears on the physical credential only after a duplicate application or eligible renewal.
The driving record must contain the actual physical address even when a different mailing address is used.
A post office box, general delivery, highway-contract route or rural route may be used as a mailing address.
A credential holder must not lend a license, instruction permit or identification card to someone else.
A person must not use another person’s license, instruction permit or identification card.
A person must not possess or display a fraudulent or altered driving credential or identification card.
A canceled license, permit or identification card must not be retained.
A vehicle owner must not give an unlicensed driver permission to drive the vehicle.
When an owner permits an unlicensed driver to drive, both are responsible for resulting crash damage, injury or death.
A Class D holder aged twenty-one or older may renew in person as early as twenty-five months before expiration.
An Idaho license renewal can run for four years, eight years or the remainder of the holder’s lawful stay.
A Class D holder aged twenty-one through sixty-two may choose the eight-year renewal.
Every license renewal requires vision screening.
Failed renewal vision screening may require an eye specialist to complete a vision examination form.
A renewal may require a medical examination form because of a prior condition or an examiner’s observation.
An Idaho or other-state Class D license expired at least twenty-five months requires the applicable knowledge and skills tests.
A lost credential found after a duplicate is issued must be destroyed or given to the county office.
The newly issued duplicate is the credential the holder should keep.
The expiration birthday is shown on the Idaho driver’s license.
A holder temporarily outside Idaho at expiration may apply for an extension of up to twelve months.
A holder who needs more time may reapply for a second and final twelve-month extension.
Active-duty United States military members and their dependents may apply for as many extensions as needed during the active-duty period.
A newcomer who lost a valid other-state credential must supply documentation to help verify identity.
An applicant must be at least fifteen to take the knowledge and skills tests.
The minimum vision standard is twenty-forty in at least one eye, with corrective lenses permitted.
Using glasses or contacts for the vision screening results in a lens restriction on the license.
A driver with a lens restriction must wear the required glasses or contacts whenever driving.
Ignoring the required lens restriction can lead to a citation and suspension of driving privileges.
A county DMV agent may require a physician’s medical form before licensing when a condition could affect safe driving.
A new applicant, an other-state transfer or a holder whose Idaho license expired at least twenty-five months must take the knowledge test.
Idaho’s knowledge-test questions draw their information from the Driver’s Handbook.
The Idaho knowledge test contains forty questions.
An applicant can miss up to six knowledge-test questions before failing.
After failing the knowledge test, an applicant must wait three days before retesting.
A failed knowledge-test attempt requires another payment of the knowledge-test fee before retesting.
C2: The knowledge and skills tests may be taken in either order.
Skills tests may be scheduled only during daylight and acceptable weather.
Twelve or fewer errors is the skills-test passing score.
A failed skills test requires a three-day wait before retesting.
A skills-test retake requires paying both the county and examiner fees again.
A person who has never been licensed must take a skills test.
A learner younger than seventeen who completed approved training and supervised instruction must take the skills test when eligible.
An instruction-permit holder aged seventeen or older needs a skills test to become licensed.
An applicant whose vision does not meet the minimum standard must take a skills test.
A recurring skills-test requirement may result from a medical or vision condition.
A foreign-license applicant must take a skills test unless a reciprocity agreement applies.
A non-commercial Idaho or other-state license expired at least twenty-five months requires a skills test.
A mental or physical impairment affecting safe driving can trigger a skills-test requirement.
A county agent’s concern about safe driving can trigger a skills test regardless of age or previous licensing experience.
Third-party contractors administer Idaho’s Class D skills tests.
An applicant needing or wanting a restricted skills test must notify the examiner.
A restricted skills test may accommodate applicants who cannot drive beyond proposed restrictions or want to travel only between specified places.
An applicant seeking an unrestricted license must complete the whole test route without modifications.
The applicant must discuss restricted-test options with the examiner before testing.
A skills-test applicant must bring photo identity evidence.
A non-owner using a vehicle for testing must give the examiner the owner’s written permission or permission spoken in person.
Permission to use the test vehicle cannot be given over the telephone.
The test vehicle must carry current insurance evidence on paper or in digital form.
An SR22 does not qualify as skills-test proof of insurance.
The test vehicle must carry current registration signed by the registrant, rather than a photocopy.
A skills-test receipt is required for identity verification only when no state-issued credential is supplied, and photo identification is still necessary.
A medical-caution reevaluation or required skills test needs the applicable ITD skills-test evaluation form at testing.
Skills-test passengers are normally prohibited, and each permitted exception passenger must be at least eighteen, carry valid identification and sign the liability waiver.
One parent or legal guardian may accompany an applicant aged seventeen or younger during a skills test if the passenger-exception requirements are met.
A translator may accompany a skills-test applicant under the passenger exception without holding translator certification or a driver’s license.
The applicant is responsible for obtaining a translator when one is needed for the skills test.
A law-enforcement officer may accompany an inmate during a skills test under the passenger exception.
A religious missionary companion may accompany the skills-test applicant when requested under the passenger exception.
The examiner inspects passenger access, passenger restraints, the required mirrors, windshield, tires and dashboard warnings before testing.
Skills-test tires must have at least two thirty-seconds of an inch of tread.
Studded tires are prohibited from May first through September thirtieth for the skills-test vehicle.
A dealer-plated vehicle may be used for a skills test only by a dealer or full-time salesperson who proves that status with a state dealer identification card.
A rental car cannot be used for the skills test by an unlicensed applicant or one younger than twenty-five.
A test vehicle that fails safety standards requires rescheduling with a roadworthy vehicle or after repairs.
The applicant must locate or demonstrate that the driver door, restraint, vehicle lights, signals, wipers, window, horn, parking brake and defroster work properly for the examiner.
The applicant must demonstrate each of the three arm signals during the vehicle-knowledge inspection.
At most three misses in the vehicle-knowledge inspection are allowed before proceeding to driving.
The skills test includes business and residential roads, curves, freeway driving, lane changes, parking lots, left and right turns, U-turns and stall and curb parking.
Skills-test scoring includes vehicle control, observation, spacing, signaling, speed, stopping, lane position, parking and right of way.
A critical driving error automatically fails the skills test and ends it immediately.
Missing the same scored skill five or more times is a critical driving error.
Parking more than eighteen inches from the curb while impeding traffic is a critical driving error.
After passing, the applicant must deliver the examiner’s sealed results envelope to the county DMV without opening it.
Results in an opened or altered test envelope are held until ITD verifies and approves them.
After a failed skills test, the examiner sends the failed result to ITD for the driving record.
Driving authority begins only after the passing skills result is recorded and the driver’s license is issued.
Controlled and uncontrolled intersections, railroad crossings and roundabouts are included in the skills test.
A dangerous action during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Disobeying an emergency or safety vehicle during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Disobeying police or safety personnel during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Disregarding a traffic sign or signal during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Driving onto a curb or sidewalk during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Examiner intervention or disobedience to the examiner during the skills test is a critical driving error.
A lane violation during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Passenger interference during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Speeding during the skills test is a critical driving error.
Striking an object during the skills test is a critical driving error.
The skills-test windshield must have no cracks or obstructions.
The test vehicle must have a rear-view mirror or both side mirrors.
Critical dashboard warning lights or gauges must not be illuminated on the skills-test vehicle.
The handbook warns that online practice tests do not accurately represent Idaho knowledge tests, apart from ITD’s own website sample questions.
